questions.question: Which of the following identity is correct regarding GNP?

options.text: GNP = GDP + Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world + Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

GNP = GDP - Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world - Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

GNP = GDP + Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world - Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

GNP = GDP - Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world + Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GNP = GDP + Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world - Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The** gross national product (GNP**) is an estimation of the** total worth of all finished goods and services** produced over a** specific time period** using resources owned by th**e citizens of a nation**.
 
• Commonly, the gross national product is determined by** adding up** all **domestic private investment, domestic government spending, net exports, and any resident income** from overseas investments, then **deducting foreign resident income.**
 
• The difference between a **country's exports and any imports** of goods and services is what is known as **net exports.**
 
• A superset of the** GDP** is the GNP.
 
• While** GDP limits its examination of the economy** to the nation's borders, GNP expands it to include the** net foreign economic activities** carried out by its citizens.
 
• GNP and GDP can have** different values**, and a significant gap between them can indicate a** country's level of economic integration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **total monetary worth** of all completed goods and services produced in a nation d**uring a given time period **is known as the **gross domestic product (GDP).**
 
• An **estimate of a nation's GDP** can be used to determine the **size and growth rate **of an economy.
 
• **Spending, output, and income** can all be used to compute GDP, which can then be adjusted for **population and inflation **to give more detailed results.
 
• **Real GDP** takes into account the **effects of inflation** while **nominal GDP** does not.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a capital expense?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Construction of school buildings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The construction of school buildings** is considered a** capital expense**.
 
• **Capital expenses** are those expenditures incurred to acquire, upgrade, or improve long-term assets, such as buildings, equipment, or land, that are expected to provide benefits over multiple accounting periods.
 
• In the context of school buildings, constructing or renovating a facility typically involves significant expenditure and is intended to provide a long-term benefit by providing a space for education and learning over many years.
 
• Therefore, the costs associated with constructing school buildings are classified as capital expenses rather than operating expenses, which are typically incurred for day-to-day operations and maintenance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pension** benefits are indeed typically classified as a non-operating expense.
 
• **Salaries expense, **payable to employees, is typically categorized as an operating expense. However, its classification as either an administrative expense or a selling expense depends on the function of the employee.
 
• **Subsidies **are considered revenue expenditures since they neither generate assets nor decrease government liabilities.

questions.question: Assessment of the country’s GDP growth, external balance and fiscal balance are presented in which part of the budget document?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is the __**Macroeconomic Framework Statement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• These statements are an integral part of the budget document in India. They provide a comprehensive overview of the country’s macroeconomic situation, including key indicators such as **GDP growth**, **external balance**, and **fiscal balance**. 
 
• The **Macroeconomic Framework Statements** outline the government’s assumptions and projections related to economic growth, inflation, fiscal deficit, and other critical factors.
 
• These statements **serve as the foundation for budget planning and policy formulation**. They help policymakers make informed decisions by understanding the broader economic context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Under the **FRBM Act**, the following documents are to be laid in both the Houses of Parliament along with the Annual Financial Statement and Demands for Grants in the budget session:

__
 
• Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement
 
• Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
 
• Macroeconomic Framework Statement

 
• 
 
**Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement**__:

 __
 
• This statement outlines the government’s fiscal policy objectives and targets for the next three years.
 
• It includes details about revenue collection, expenditure priorities, and debt management.
 
• The **Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement** provides transparency and accountability by setting clear fiscal goals and strategies.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement**__:

 __
 
• This statement complements the **Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement**.
 
• It outlines the government’s strategic priorities regarding taxation, subsidies, public expenditure, and debt management.
 
• The **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement** helps align fiscal policies with broader economic goals and ensures consistency in decision-making.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**__** Appropriation Bill**__:

 
• While not directly related to the assessment of economic indicators, the **Appropriation Bill is a crucial part of the budget process.**
 
• It authorizes the government to **withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet its expenses during the financial year**.
 
• Essentially, it allows the government to **allocate funds for various programs, projects, and administrative functions**.

questions.question: According to the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, in how many categories were the industries classified in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 **was a protestation of the major part played by the Government sector in the process of the growth of industrialization.
 
• **The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956,** formed the base of the alternate **five-time plan (1956- 1961) of the planning commission.**
 
• Under this, diligence was classified into three orders, which are popularly known as the top rudiments of **IPR- 1956:**
 
 
• **The three-fold classification of industries: **This element divided industries into three categories namely;
 
 
• **Schedule A:** Industries that are exclusively owned by the state.
 
• **Schedule B:** Industries can be under the private sector, but the starting of the new units will be under the public sector control.
 
• **Schedule C:** Some industries will be under the private sector, but these have to take a license from the public sector.
 
 
 
• **Industrial License:** This is also known as Permit License Raj, under this element, no new industry was allowed to be set up unless a license was obtained from the Government.
 
 
• This policy was used for promoting industrialization in backward regions because it was easier to obtain a license if the industrial unit was established in an economically backward area to promote regional equality.
 
• Even any existing industry had to obtain a license for expanding or diversifying its production.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Concessions:** Industrial units were given concessions such as tax benefits and electricity at a lower rate to encourage establishing their units in the country’s backward region.
 
 
• This was done to promote regional equality.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IPR-1956, **focused on the role of the Government in** boosting the industrial sector by classifying them into different categories, **imposing licensing as a mandatory measure to open or expand any industry and providing concessions like discounts to lure more industries setting up in the backward region.

questions.question: In 2011–12, what percentage of Indian workforce was engaged in secondary sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **24.3%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Manufacturing and industry:** The secondary sector encompasses activities related to the processing of raw materials into finished goods, including manufacturing, construction, and mining.
 
• **Economic growth:** The secondary sector plays a crucial role in economic growth and development, as it generates jobs and contributes to exports.
 
• **Shift from agriculture:** Over time, there has been a shift in India's workforce from the primary sector (agriculture) to the secondary sector, reflecting industrialization and modernization.
 
• **Challenges and opportunities:** The secondary sector in India faces challenges such as competition from other countries, infrastructure bottlenecks, and labor shortages. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary sector:** Agriculture remains the primary source of employment for a significant portion of India's population, particularly in rural areas.
 
• **Tertiary sector:** The tertiary sector, also known as the service sector, is growing rapidly in India and now accounts for the largest share of employment. 
 
• **Regional variations:** The distribution of the workforce across different sectors varies across different regions of India. 
 
• **Informal sector:** A significant portion of India's workforce is engaged in the informal sector, which includes small-scale enterprises and self-employment.

questions.question: Priorities of the government in the fiscal area and its related policies and deviations are mentioned in which part of the budget document?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement:-**

 
 
• **The priorities of the government in the fiscal area and its related policies and deviations are mentioned in the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement section of the budget document.**
 
• This section outlines the government's strategic priorities for the ensuing financial year, including its plans for taxation, expenditure, lending and investments, administered pricing, borrowings, and guarantees.
 
• It also discusses any deviations from previous fiscal measures and provides justification for these deviations.
 
• **The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement is mandated by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 (FRBMA).**
 
• The FRBMA is an Indian law that aims to achieve sustainable fiscal management in the country. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Appropriation bill:-**

 
 
• **It is also known as a supply bill or spending bill, is a proposed law that authorizes the expenditure of government funds. **
 
• It is a bill that sets money aside for specific spending. In some democracies, approval of the legislature is necessary for the government to spend money.
 
• In a Westminster parliamentary system, the defeat of an appropriation bill in a parliamentary vote generally necessitates either the resignation of a government or the calling of a general election.
 
 
 
• **Macroeconomic Framework Statement:-**
 
 
• **MFS is an official document presented by the government that provides an overview of the macroeconomic outlook for the coun**try.
 
• It outlines the government's assessment of the current economic situation and its projections for future economic performance.
 
• The MFS also outlines the government's fiscal policy stance, which includes plans for taxation, expenditure, and borrowing.
 
 
 
• **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement:-**
 
 
• **MTFPS is a fiscal policy document that outlines the government's fiscal strategy for the medium term, typically three to five years.**
 
• It provides a framework for managing the government's finances and achieving its fiscal objectives, such as controlling deficits, reducing debt, and promoting sustainable economic growth.

questions.question: Trade liberalisation has helped India improve its _____________ in industries with medium-to-high technology content.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**comparative advantage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trade liberalization** has played a pivotal role in **enhancing India's comparative advantage** in industries with medium-to-high technology content.
 
• Initiated in the 1980s, the process of trade liberalization in India underwent a radical transformation in 1991, marked by a program aimed at gradually reducing tariffs.
 
• The effects of trade liberalization on employment in India have been substantial, ushering in new job prospects and bolstering economic expansion.
 
• The liberalization of markets and heightened trade activities have spurred job growth across various sectors, including manufacturing, services, and export-oriented industries. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Trade liberalization** entails the elimination or reduction of constraints or impediments on the unrestricted flow of goods between nations.
 
• Such barriers encompass tariffs, including duties and surcharges, as well as non-tariff barriers like licensing regulations and quotas.
 
• Economists typically perceive the relaxation or removal of these constraints as measures to advance free trade.
 
• Trade liberalization facilitates free trade, enabling countries to engage in the exchange of goods without regulatory impediments or associated expenses.

questions.question: What is the reason behind most people working in the agricultural sector?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As countries develop, the share of the population working in agriculture is declining.
 
• While further than two-thirds of the population in poor countries work in agriculture, lower than 5 of the population does in rich countries.
 
• It's generally the huge productivity increase that makes this reduction in labor possible.
 
• Also, productivity earnings make it possible to reduce the agrarian land demanded to feed a given number of people.
 
• People didn't get higher returns in agriculture. Instead, they involve in agriculture because there is no experience required and also no qualification.
 
• The main reason is unemployment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sectors in Economy:**

 
 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• To keep the day-to-day operations going, this sector's services are completely reliant on the availability of natural resources.
 
• Eg. Agriculture, Mining, Fishing, Forestry, Dairy, etc. 
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• The economics of the sector is based on natural materials that are utilized to manufacture the services and goods that are given, and which are then consumed.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• The tertiary sector is referred to as the service sector.
 
• The service business creates services rather than finished items.
 
• Services (also known as "Intangible Products") include things like attention, direction, access, experience, and emotional labor.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true with regard to the Green Revolution?

options.text: Cultivation became more intensive in nature.
Cultivation became more extensive in nature.
In its second phase, there was a shift to from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation in dry and semi-arid regions of India.
There was change in the cropping pattern and types of crops grown in its second phase.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cultivation became more extensive in nature**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cultivation became more extensive in nature**:

 
 
• This is **NOT** true.
 
• **The Green Revolution focused on intensifying agricultur**e (increasing output per acre), rather than extending farming to more land.
 
• It did not involve expanding farmland but rather improving productivity on existing farmland.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Green Revolution led to more intensive farming practices, where farmers used high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds,**

 
 
• **chemical fertilizers, and irrigation to maximize crop production per unit of land.**
 
• Hence this is true
 
 
 
• The** second phase of the Green Revolution saw the spread of irrigated farming to dry and semi-arid regions**, which helped in increasing productivity.
 
 
• Hence this is also true
 
 
 
• In the second phase, **the Green Revolution included a shift to different crops, especially from cereals like wheat and rice to more diverse crops, including oilseeds and pulses.**
 
 
• So this is also true

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Recoveries of loans and advances**, borrowings, are an example of **capital receipts**.
 
• **Capital receipts **encompass funds received by the government that either **create liabilities or reduce financial** assets.
 
• They represent incoming cash flows and can be categorized as both non-debt and debt receipts.
 
• Examples of capital receipts include loans obtained from the general public, foreign governments, and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• Additionally, borrowings from foreign countries and institutions, as well as borrowings from the RBI, are considered capital receipts.
 
• The recovery of loans extended by the central government to states and other entities also falls under this category.
 
• On the balance sheet, capital receipts are typically listed in the liabilities section. It's important to note that capital receipts generally do not recur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-tax revenue **constitutes income generated by the government from sources other than taxes. These receipts include earnings from various sources such as interest on loans, dividends on investments (e.g., from Public Sector Undertakings), fees, and revenues from services provided by the government.
 
• **Revenue receipts** represent the income derived by a business from its routine operational activities. These receipts are recurring and directly impact the profit and loss statement of the business.
 
• **Tax revenue, **on the other hand, refers to the total receipts generated by the government from taxes and other duties.

questions.question: Shifting agriculture is known as ______ in the Western Ghats.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Kumari.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shifting cultivation, under the names Kumari**, Hakkal, or Punam( local names). It has been an important agricultural system in the Western Ghats.
 
• **Shifting cultivation** is a form of agricultural practice in which farmers clear an area of land by slashing vegetation and burning forests for agricultural purposes.
 
• This practice is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture or slash-and-burn cultivation.
 
• **Jhum or Jhoom cultivation** is also known as shifting cultivation or cultivation or slash and burn cultivation.
 
• **Jhum cultivation** was practised in Central Highland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Shifting Cultivation Process **

 
• Each year farmers choose an area for planting.
 
• They have to remove vegetation that typically covers the land.
 
• They cut most of the trees with the help of axes, which are economically helpful.
 
• In different regions, the cleared area is called Swidden, Ladang, milpa, Chena, and Kaingin.
 
• They cultivate the cleared land only briefly, usually three or fewer seasons.
 
• Farmers leave the old site uncropped for 10 to 25 years.
 
• They will return to the land after 10 to 20 years to cultivate again.

questions.question: What is an indicator of self-reliance?

options.text: Increase in imports of the goods which could be produced in the country.
Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country.
Increase in exports of the goods which could not be produced in the country.
Avoiding exports of the goods which could be produced in the country.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A self-reliant economy is one that does not require any aid, support, interaction or trade with the outside world**.
 
• Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country will utilise the available resources within the country and will lower the burden to borrow from outside the country. **Hence it is an indicator of being self-reliant**.
 
• An increase in imports of the goods which could be produced in the country will increase the burden of the country to borrow from other countries. **Hence it is not an indicator of Self-reliance**.
 
• An increase in exports of goods which could not be produced in the country will create an extra burden on the economy of the country.** Hence it is not an indicator of Self - reliance**.
 
• Avoiding exports of the goods which could be produced in the country will lose the chance of strengthening the economy of the country. **Hence it is not an indicator of Self - reliance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (meaning self-reliant India scheme) was announced in four tranches by the Union Finance Minister** Nirmala Sitharaman in May 2020**.
 
• The Prime Minister announced that an Atmanirbhar Bharat or a self-reliant India should stand on the following five pillars
 
 
• Economy
 
• Infrastructure
 
• 21st-century technology-driven arrangements and system
 
• Demand
 
• Vibrant Demography

questions.question: Why are the intermediate goods NOT included in the National Income?

options.text: For the prevention of double accounting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For the prevention of double accounting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intermediate goods** are not included in the National Income to prevent double accounting.
 
• Including intermediate goods would lead to **double counting** because their value is already embedded in the final goods and services.
 
• National Income is a measure of the total value of **final goods and services** produced in an economy over a specific period.
 
• Counting intermediate goods separately would **inflate the National Income** figures inaccurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Intermediate goods are those goods that are used as inputs to produce other goods and services.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and parts used in manufacturing.
 
• Final goods are those that are ready for consumption or investment and are included in the calculation of National Income.
 
• To accurately measure the economic activity and avoid overestimation, only the value of final goods and services is counted.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an advantage of privatisation?

options.text: Additional source of revenue for the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduced competition**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reduced competition** is not considered an advantage of privatisation.
 
• Privatisation typically aims to increase competition by introducing private players into sectors previously dominated by state-run enterprises.
 
• Increased competition can lead to better services, more innovation, and greater efficiency in the market.
 
• Other advantages of privatisation include generating additional revenue for the government, reducing political interference, and improving overall performance of the enterprises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership, property or business from the government to the private sector.
 
• It is often part of broader economic reforms aimed at improving efficiency and productivity.
 
• Privatisation can also help in reducing the fiscal burden on the government and in fostering a more competitive economic environment.
 
• However, it is important to carefully regulate privatised sectors to ensure fair competition and prevent monopolistic practices.

questions.question: Identify the crop which is grown in Kharif cropping season in Northern States of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rice** is predominantly grown during the Kharif cropping season in Northern States of India.
 
• The Kharif cropping season typically starts with the onset of the monsoon in June and lasts until October.
 
• Rice requires a hot and humid climate with substantial rainfall, which aligns with the conditions during the Kharif season in Northern India.
 
• Other crops grown in the Kharif season include maize, sorghum, and pulses, but rice is the most significant among them.
 
• States such as Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar are major producers of Kharif rice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** significantly boosted rice production in Northern India, particularly in Punjab and Haryana.
 
• Rice is a staple food for a large part of the Indian population, especially in the eastern and southern regions.
 
• The government provides various subsidies and support mechanisms to encourage rice cultivation during the Kharif season.
 
• Modern agricultural practices and irrigation facilities have further enhanced rice yield in these regions.

questions.question:
Calculate the GDP at factor cost given in the following data.

GDP at market price = 600 crores

Consumption of fixed capital = 100 crores

Indirect taxes = 200 crores

Subsidies = 50 crores
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **450 Crores**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **GDP at factor cost **is calculated by **adjusting the GDP at market price for indirect taxes and subsidies.**
 
• According to these questions,​
 
 
• **GDP at Market Price** = ₹600 crores
 
• **Consumption of Fixed Capital** (Depreciation) = ₹100 crores
 
• **Indirect Taxes** = ₹200 crores
 
• **Subsidies** = ₹50 crores
 
• The** formula is GDP at factor cost = GDP at market price - Indirect taxes + Subsidies.**
 
• 
 
Using the given values, we get:

 
⇒ 600 crores - 200 crores + 50 crores = 450 crores.

 
 
• 
 
Therefore,** the ****GDP at factor cost is ₹450 crores.**

questions.question: In 1950-51, what percentage of GDP of India was contributed by the industrial sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 percent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** industrial policy** that India developed was closely tied to **trade law.**
 
• Trade was characterized in th**e first seven plans **by what is referred to as an** internal trading strategy.**
 
• This tactic is known as** import substitution technically.**
 
• This approach attempted to** supplement indigenous** production with** imports.**
 
• The government shielded indigenous industries from** foreign competition under this policy**.
 
• **Two methods **were used to prevent imports:** tariffs, and quotas.**
 
• Tariffs are a charge on **imported goods;** they raise the cost of** imports and reduce demand** for them.
 
• The amount of merchandise that may be** imported is determined by quotas.**
 
• **Industrial sector contributions to GDP** increased throughout this time, going from **13% in 1950–1951 to 24.6% in 2016.**
 
• A key development indicator is the **growth in the industry's GDP share. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Economic Survey document is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) under the guidance of the Chief Economic Advisor.
 
• It is usually presented a day before the Union Budget is presented in Parliament.
 
• The first Economic Survey in India was presented in the year 1950- 51.
 
• Up to 1964, it was presented along with the Union Budget. From 1964 onwards, it has been delinked from the Budget.

questions.question: Which of the following is an indirect tax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GST **(Goods and Services Tax) is an **indirect tax**.
 
• It is levied on the **supply of goods and services**.
 
• **GST **introduced in India on **July 1, 2017**.
 
• **GST replaces **various **indirect taxes** like **VAT, excise duty, and service tax**.
 
• It is charged at **each stage **of the **production and distribution chain**.
 
• Ultimately, the burden of **GST** is passed on to the end consumer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Death duty**

 
 
• **Death duty** is a tax on assets transferred upon an **individual's death**.
 
• It's also referred to as **inheritance or estate tax**.
 
 
 
• **Interest tax** 
 
 
• **Interest tax **is levied on **interest income earned** from investments.
 
• It's a form of **direct tax **imposed by governments.
 
• Tax rates on interest income vary based on **jurisdiction and tax status**.
 
 
 
• **Capital gains tax**
 
 
• **Capital gains tax **is imposed on **profits from selling capital assets**.
 
• It applies when the** selling price exceeds** the **original purchase price**.
 
• It's a form of **direct tax**, paid by the taxpayer.
